# Terse

> Terse puts everything on your desktop wallpaper. It is a live 3D particle wallpaper for macOS and Windows that rebuilds your own desktop picture out of particles and writes what is happening on your computer into it: the synced lyrics of the song you are playing (Music mode), notifications from every app, window titles, what your AI coding agents are doing, and Code Town, a first-person particle town. For developers it is also an on-device AI agent butler that cuts token costs by 40-70%: it compresses prompts, live-monitors 8 coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cline, Windsurf, OpenClaw, Aider), caps runaway spend with a budget circuit breaker, manages MCP servers and diagnoses token waste with Terse Doctor. Everything runs on-device. Also available as a Chrome extension and a VS Code extension.

## Key Facts
- Live particle wallpaper: your own desktop picture rebuilt as a 3D particle field; notifications, window titles, Now Playing and agent activity condense out of it as text, hold, and dissolve. New sources are detected automatically, each with its own switch
- Music mode (free): recognises the playing song from the system's Now Playing (Apple Music, Spotify, NetEase Cloud Music and most players), fetches synced lyrics (.lrc next to the file, embedded tags, LRCLIB, NetEase) and draws each line as particles on the wallpaper. Lyrics are line-timed, not per-word. No audio is recorded. Pro adds floating lyrics above all windows and 15 appearance controls
- Wallpaper engines and Pro styles: cinematic particle typography, Orbit Burst rings, the Chladni plate, eight styles and ten themes, a 3D free view, always-on-top, and on-device hand-gesture control (Apple Vision)
- Code Town: the plaza's first-person particle town as a wallpaper; every villa is a project someone published
- Reduces token usage 40-70% on verbose prompts; 35+ on-device optimization techniques (<5ms)
- Live monitoring of 8 agents: input/output tokens, cache read/write efficiency, per-turn cost (model-aware pricing), burn rate, context-window fill
- Budget circuit breaker: burn-rate / token / dollar ceilings that escalate from alert to pausing (SIGSTOP) or killing (SIGTERM) the agent process before the next API call
- MCP Manager: discovers every MCP server across Claude Code / Cursor / Windsurf configs; risk-scores each (remote transport, embedded credentials, code-execution surface, unpinned supply chain); enable/disable without editing JSON
- Terse Doctor: ~25 consent-gated scans — cache thrash, duplicate tool calls, redundant file reads, context burn, CLAUDE.md token tax, secret exposure, runaway runtimes — with one-click fixes
- 3 optimization modes: Soft (typo-fix only), Normal (filler removal), Aggressive (max compression); code blocks always protected
- Alert Center: macOS/Windows notifications, Slack webhook, ntfy.sh push; weekly savings digest
- Team sharing: publish live agent sessions and aggregate stats to teammates
- Pricing: free tier, plus a 30-day free trial on both paid tiers. Terse Pro $4.99/mo (also weekly $1.99, quarterly $12, yearly $15.99, lifetime $25.99 — same plan, same entitlement); Terse Premium $99/mo for teams (unlimited sessions and devices, full analytics, priority support). macOS + Windows, built with Tauri + Rust + Swift. The Terse SDK on GitHub is MIT licensed and free.

## Pricing
- Free: 30-day trial, all 3 modes, spell correction
- Monthly ($4.99/mo): Unlimited optimizations, agent monitoring, budget circuit breaker, MCP manager, Doctor, CLAUDE.md generation
